gcp-pcd-s1.1-09.reason: ambiguous: 'share process-level state' is wrong for multi-process servers. Now states the documented fact: Cloud Run gives no isolation between concurrent requests. (final: keep)
gcp-pcd-s1.1-09.statement: Cloud Run leaves isolation between concurrent requests in one service instance to the application code.
gcp-pcd-s1.1-09.explanation: With concurrency above 1, Cloud Run provides no isolation between requests one instance processes at once. Shared mutable state, such as globals in a threaded server, needs concurrency-safe code.

gcp-pcd-s1.1-07.reason: tell: removes the control verb 'enforce' (7 of 7 such verbs were on false cards). Same fact, same answer. (final: keep)
gcp-pcd-s1.1-07.statement: Cloud Run keeps configured traffic percentages for returning clients when session affinity is enabled.
gcp-pcd-s1.1-07.explanation: Cloud Run's best-effort session affinity takes precedence over traffic splits. Returning clients can skew the observed proportions across revisions.
gcp-pcd-s1.1-07.misconception: Session affinity preserves configured traffic proportions for returning clients.

gcp-pcd-s1.2-01.statement: Attaching a user-managed service identity to a Cloud Run service requires the deployer to hold actAs on that account.
gcp-pcd-s1.2-01.explanation: The deployer needs iam.serviceAccounts.actAs on the service account, for example through the Service Account User role, to attach it to a Cloud Run service or revision.

gcp-pcd-s1.3-02.reason: ambiguous: 'that query' had nothing to refer to, and 'requires' suggested a query error. Now states the silent exclusion. Page: 'An orderBy() clause also filters for existence of the given field. The result set will not include documents that do not contain the given field.' (final: keep)
gcp-pcd-s1.3-02.statement: A Firestore query ordered by a field omits documents that lack that field, even when they match its filters.
gcp-pcd-s1.3-02.explanation: In Firestore, an orderBy clause also filters on the field's existence, so documents without the field drop out of results silently. Give every document the field or run a separate query.

gcp-pcd-s2.1-09.reason: explanation_error: Node.js handlers declare their type through functions.http or functions.cloudEvent registration, not only through a configured flag. Statement and answer are unchanged. The source moves to the page that shows the registration and says code 'must specify one of the two signature types'. (final: keep)
gcp-pcd-s2.1-09.statement: The Node.js Functions Framework detects HTTP or CloudEvent signatures from handler parameters.
gcp-pcd-s2.1-09.explanation: Node.js code declares the signature type by registering its handler with functions.http or functions.cloudEvent. The framework does not read the handler's parameter list to decide.
gcp-pcd-s2.1-09.misconception: The Node.js Functions Framework infers the trigger signature from the handler's parameters.

gcp-pcd-s2.2-05.statement: Cloud Build supplies $SHORT_SHA as a default substitution to builds that a trigger invokes.
gcp-pcd-s2.2-05.explanation: Trigger-invoked builds get default substitutions such as $COMMIT_SHA and $SHORT_SHA. A build started with gcloud builds submit gets these values only when the developer passes them.

gcp-pcd-s2.3-03.explanation: Pub/Sub events carry base64-encoded data values, and the function is expected to decode them. A local sample event therefore needs base64-encoded data as well.

gcp-pcd-s2.3-04.explanation: Because steps share that network, they can communicate: an integration-test step can call a service container that an earlier step started on the cloudbuild network.

gcp-pcd-s2.3-05.statement: Cloud Build's allowExitCodes takes precedence over allowFailure in a test step that sets both.
gcp-pcd-s2.3-05.explanation: With allowFailure true and allowExitCodes [1], a test step that exits with 2 still fails the build, because only the listed exit codes are tolerated.

gcp-pcd-s3.2-07.explanation: Prometheus Adapter queries are global in scope, so identically named metrics from other namespaces feed the HPA. Add namespace or cluster filters to the PromQL query.

gcp-pcd-s4.1-01.reason: weak_card: 'SDK retries' gave away the repeat. Now tests the external side effect of a rerun callback. Page: a transaction function 'might run more than once if a concurrent edit affects a document that the transaction reads' and 'should not directly modify application state'. (final: keep)
gcp-pcd-s4.1-01.statement: A Firestore server SDK transaction callback that sends an email can send it twice for one commit.
gcp-pcd-s4.1-01.explanation: Server client libraries rerun the whole transaction callback after contention, while Firestore's atomic commit covers only database writes. Return data from the callback and send email after it succeeds.

gcp-pcd-s4.1-03.reason: weak_card: near-copy of the source sentence, and the concessive 'even with' hinted at True. Page: 'Mobile and web SDKs emulate optimistic concurrency transactions using write preconditions on document versions. This emulation occurs regardless of the database's concurrency mode setting.' (final: keep)
gcp-pcd-s4.1-03.statement: A Firestore web SDK transaction checks document versions at commit rather than locking the documents it reads.
gcp-pcd-s4.1-03.explanation: Mobile and web SDKs emulate optimistic concurrency with write preconditions on document versions, so they behave optimistically even when the database concurrency mode is PESSIMISTIC.

gcp-pcd-s4.1-05.reason: weak_card (generic database truism). Now tests the documented Cloud SQL point: the application, not the pool, retries. Page: 'If errors happen in the middle of a transaction, the application must do the retrying, and it must retry from the beginning of a transaction. So even if your pool is configured properly, the application might still see errors if connections are lost.' (final: keep)
gcp-pcd-s4.1-05.statement: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL apps need their own retry logic for a transaction cut off by a lost connection.
gcp-pcd-s4.1-05.explanation: Pools and backoff help when opening a connection, but the application must retry a transaction interrupted mid-way from its beginning; a well-configured pool still surfaces lost connections.

gcp-pcd-s4.2-07.reason: tell: removes 'override' (a control verb found only on false cards). Same fact and answer. Page: 'Cloud Storage ignores this header and sets response Cache-Control headers based on the stored metadata values.' (final: keep)
gcp-pcd-s4.2-07.statement: Cloud Storage sets a download's Cache-Control response header from the caller's Cache-Control request header.
gcp-pcd-s4.2-07.explanation: Cloud Storage derives a download's Cache-Control response header from the object's stored metadata. It ignores the caller's Cache-Control request header when setting that response value.
gcp-pcd-s4.2-07.misconception: The download request's caching header overrides Cloud Storage's stored object caching metadata.

gcp-pcd-s4.2-09.reason: explanation_error: the old explanation gave no recovery step and made an absolute 'stays invalid' claim. The new explanation teaches the documented recovery: a 412 lets you request the current metadata and generation before a new conditional request. Statement and answer are unchanged. (final: keep)
gcp-pcd-s4.2-09.statement: A Cloud Storage client fixes an HTTP 412 generation mismatch by retrying the request with the same precondition.
gcp-pcd-s4.2-09.explanation: A 412 means the object no longer matches the precondition. Request its current metadata, decide whether the change still applies, then send a new request with the current generation.
gcp-pcd-s4.2-09.misconception: A precondition mismatch is a transient failure resolved by resending the same stale condition.

gcp-pcd-s4.3-10.reason: tell plus source: removes 'supports' (3 of 3 uses were on false cards). Same fact and answer. The source moves from the concepts table, whose flattened layout misreads, to the Node.js page that states 'Profile types for Node.js: Heap, Wall time'. (final: keep)
gcp-pcd-s4.3-10.statement: Cloud Profiler's Node.js agent collects CPU-time profiles for diagnosing slow production handlers.
gcp-pcd-s4.3-10.explanation: Cloud Profiler offers heap and wall-time profiles for Node.js, not CPU time. A wall-time profile also counts time a handler spends waiting.
gcp-pcd-s4.3-10.misconception: The Cloud Profiler Node.js agent offers the same CPU-time profile type as its Go or Java agents.
